results.reason: Same root cause: withdraw(assets) uses floor division for shares to burn, so small withdrawals burn 0 shares when the share price is above 1.
Classic first-depositor inflation: raw-balance totalAssets, a donation, and round-down deposits minting 0 shares.
stake() updates the global accumulator but not the user's paid index, so a new stake is credited past rewards.
The price-source setter (setPair) has no owner check, so anyone can install a malicious oracle.
Collateral is priced from spot getReserves(), and a donation plus sync() moves the price in the same transaction to over-borrow.

Push-payment loop over immutable recipients where one reverting transfer (for example a blacklisted address) blocks every distribution. The extra triggers (zero amount, address(0), gas) are the same root cause.
There is no liquidation mechanism, so bad debt accumulates after price moves.

Same theme (division by zero in share conversion), but the divisor and condition differ: totalAssets==0 with totalSupply>0 here, versus totalSupply==0 on an empty vault in PA-11. It is also a follow-on of C01.
No disclosure covers emissions lost during zero-stake periods or rounding-to-zero accumulator updates, including stake(0) griefing.

The main issue matches PA-09: input measured as balance minus reserves can be stolen between transactions. The uint112 truncation in sync() is a separate sub-issue with no prior art and could be split out as novel.
No disclosure covers the unbounded, duplicate-filled borrowers array or the wrong borrowerCount.
Shares the admin reward-rate theme, but the root cause is different: checked-arithmetic overflow freezes every path, including principal withdrawal, rather than an unfunded rate.
Rewards accrue at a rate not backed by funded balance, so late claimers' all-or-nothing claims revert. Its secondary stake-checkpoint driver duplicates PA-02 (and C03).
Output is transferred before reserves update, with no lock, so a hook-bearing token can re-enter swap and reuse the same input.
The nominal amount is credited instead of the received balance delta, so fee-on-transfer deposits are over-credited.

Shares the pair-reserve oracle dependency, but the root cause is different: price() reverts when reserve0==0, which freezes collateral withdrawal even for users with no debt. It does not rely on PA-05's setter.

notes: 10 duplicates (C01-C07, C10, C13-C15), 3 related (C08, C12, C16), 2 novel (C09, C11). C10's uint112 sync-truncation sub-issue has no prior art and could be split out as novel. C13 overlaps C03 and PA-02 through its stake-checkpoint driver; its distinct claim-insolvency aspect maps to PA-07. C08 is a consequence of C01 and C16 overlaps C04's revert-griefing variant, so the triager may treat both as follow-ons within this batch.
